info.title: Fiber AI API
info.description:
# Welcome to the Fiber AI API!



Get your API key at <https://fiber.ai/app/api>.

## Authentication

Include your API key in **one** of the following ways (listed in priority order):

**Option 1 — Request body (POST) or query params (GET):**
```json
{
"apiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY"
}
```

For a GET request, you can include your API key in the query params like this:
```
?apiKey=YOUR_API_KEY
```

**Option 2 — `x-api-key` header:**
```
x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
```

**Option 3 — `Authorization` header (Bearer token):**
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

If an API key is provided in both the body/query and a header, the body/query value takes precedence.

## Rate limits

Each endpoint has its own rate limit, and if you exceed it you will get a '429' error. Please contact us if you'd like to request a higher rate limit.

## Client timeouts

Some sync endpoints perform live data fetches or multi-step enrichment and can take longer than the default HTTP client timeout (often 30s). Endpoints that require extra time display a **Recommended timeout** badge in their documentation. Configure your HTTP client's timeout to at least the recommended value before calling those endpoints to avoid premature connection drops.

## Troubleshooting

Need help? Write to adi@fiber.ai or your contact on the Fiber team.

# SDKs & MCP

Integrate the Fiber API into your applications with official SDKs or via **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) for LLM and AI agents.

- **[Fiber SDKs](https://docs.fiber.ai/article/fiber-sdks)** — Client libraries and usage guides for your language or framework.
- **[Using MCP in LLMs](https://docs.fiber.ai/article/using-mcp-in-llms)** — Connect Claude, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible tools to Fiber.
- **[Developing with AI agents](https://docs.fiber.ai/article/developing-with-ai-agents)** — Plugins, MCP servers, skills, and quickstart for building with Fiber in your IDE.

---

post.description: Poll for the results of a social media lookup task. ⚡ Rate limit: 20 requests per 1 minute

platform.description: The social media platform this candidate is for.

handle.description: The handle or username on that platform, without any @ prefix (e.g. 'karpathy').

profileUrl.description: Full URL to the profile on that platform (e.g. 'https://x.com/karpathy').

displayName.description: The display name shown on the profile.

location.description: Location as displayed on the profile.

followerCount.description: Number of followers on that platform.

isVerified.description: Whether the account is verified on that platform.

confidenceOutOf10.description: Confidence score from 0 to 10. Higher scores indicate a stronger match.

rationale.description: The AI reasoning for why this profile was selected as the best match.

candidates.description: The best-match profiles found, one per platform. Empty if no confident matches were found.

errorMessage.description: Error message if the lookup failed for this person.

data.description: The lookup results for each person in this run.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page of results. Null if there are no more results.

hasMore.description: Whether there are more results to fetch.

post.description: Search for investors with flexible filtering capabilities ⚡ Rate limit: 30 requests per 1 minute 💰 Cost: 3 credits per investor found ⓘ

countryCode.description: Country or region filter with include/exclude pattern. Region codes like X-ANGLOSPHERE expand to multiple countries (USA, GBR, AUS, etc.)

stateName.description: State name filter with include/exclude pattern. Use full state names (e.g., 'California', 'England', 'New York'). State codes like 'CA' or 'NY' are not accepted.

investorType.description: Filter by investor type: 'person' for individuals, 'organization' for firms, 'either' to include both types. Pass null/undefined to include both types (same as 'either')

types.description: Investor types filter with include/exclude pattern. Examples: include: ['venture_capital', 'angel']

numLeadInvestments.description: Filter by number of lead investments (range)

leadRate.description: Filter by lead investment rate (0.0 - 1.0). Values outside [0,1] will be clamped to this range

lastInvestmentDate.description: Filter by last investment date (date range)

foundedOn.description: Filter by founded date (date range). Note: many investors have null founded_on, so this filter may exclude many rows

field.description: Field to sort by. For 'importance', higher values indicate a more important investor (as determined by our AI). Use DESC direction to start with the most important investors.

direction.description: Sort order - asc or desc (defaults to desc)

sorting.description: Sorting configuration. If provided, field is required. Defaults to total_investment_count DESC if not provided.

isTopVc.description: Filter by whether investor is a top VC. Note: only a few dozen companies qualify as 'top'

domains.description: Array of investor domains to filter by

namePatterns.description: An array of name patterns used for partial, case-insensitive matching against investor names

crunchbaseSlugs.description: Array of Crunchbase slugs to filter by (exact match). Slugs are the last part of the Crunchbase URL (for example, 'sequoia-capital' from crunchbase.com/organization/sequoia-capital)

pageSize.description: Number of investors to return per page (max 1000)

cursor.description: Pagination cursor returned from a previous search response. Use this to fetch the next page of results. Null for the first page.

x-credit-cost.description: 3 credits per investor found

name.description: Investor name

type.description: Investor type: 'person' for individuals, 'organization' for firms

isTopVc.description: Whether investor is a top VC

domain.description: Investor domain

shareOfPortfolio.description: Share of total investments accounted for by this stage (0.0 - 1.0)

lastInvestmentDate.description: Date of most recent investment at this stage

orgLinkedinSlug.description: LinkedIn slug for the organization invested in (in long format, e.g., 'company/companyname')

orgName.description: Name of the organization invested in

roundType.description: Type of funding round (e.g., series_a, seed)

wasLeadInvestor.description: Whether the investor was lead investor

investors.description: Array of investors matching the search criteria

nextCursor.description: Cursor for fetching the next page of results. Null if no more results available

post.description: Search for investments with flexible filtering capabilities. Supports filtering by investor, company, round type, location, and financial metrics. ⚡ Rate limit: 30 requests per 1 minute 💰 Cost: 2 credits per investment found ⓘ

investorName.description: Filter by investor name (partial match, case-insensitive). Use ILIKE pattern matching.

investorType.description: Filter by investor type: 'person' for individuals, 'organization' for firms, 'either' to include both types. Pass null/undefined to include both types (same as 'either')

investorCountryCode.description: Investor country or region filter with include/exclude pattern. Region codes like X-ANGLOSPHERE expand to multiple countries (USA, GBR, AUS, etc.)

investorDomain.description: Filter by investor domain (exact match). For example, 'techstars.com' to find all investments made by Techstars

investorCrunchbaseSlug.description: Filter by investor Crunchbase slug (exact match). For example, 'sequoia-capital' to find all investments made by Sequoia Capital

companyName.description: Filter by company name (partial match, case-insensitive). Use ILIKE pattern matching.

companyLinkedinUrl.description: Filter by company LinkedIn URL. Accepts either full URL (e.g., 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/fiber-ai/') or slug (e.g., 'fiber-ai'). You can also use LinkedIn organization ID in the slug (e.g., 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/123456789/' or just '123456789')

roundType.description: Round type filter with include/exclude pattern. Examples: include: ['series_a', 'seed']

roundDate.description: Filter by funding round announcement date (date range)

raisedAmountUSD.description: Filter by amount raised in USD (range). For example, min: 5000000 to find rounds with at least $5M raised

postMoneyValuationUSD.description: Filter by post-money valuation in USD (range)

countryCode.description: Round location country or region filter with include/exclude pattern. Region codes like X-ANGLOSPHERE expand to multiple countries (USA, GBR, AUS, etc.)

stateName.description: Round location state name filter with include/exclude pattern. Use full state names (e.g., 'California', 'England', 'New York'). State codes like 'CA' or 'NY' are not accepted.

city.description: Filter by round location city (partial match, case-insensitive). Use ILIKE pattern matching.

wasLeadInvestor.description: Filter by whether the investor was a lead investor in the round

minInvestorCount.description: Filter by minimum number of investors in the funding round

direction.description: Sort order - asc or desc (defaults to desc)

sorting.description: Sorting configuration. If provided, field is required. Defaults to round_date DESC if not provided.

searchParams.description: Investment search filter parameters. If not provided, returns all investments (subject to pagination)

pageSize.description: Number of investments to return per page (max 100)

cursor.description: Pagination cursor returned from a previous search response. Use this to fetch the next page of results. Null for the first page.

x-credit-cost.description: 2 credits per investment found

roundType.description: Type of funding round (e.g., series_a, seed)

name.description: Company name

domain.description: Company domain

linkedinUrl.description: Full LinkedIn URL for the company. Examples: 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/fiber-ai/' or 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/123456789/' (using organization ID)

linkedinId.description: LinkedIn organization ID

name.description: Investor name

linkedinUrl.description: Full LinkedIn URL for the investor. Examples: 'https://www.linkedin.com/in/johndoe/' for person or 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/sequoia-capital/' for organization. You can also use organization ID (e.g., 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/123456789/')

isLeadInvestor.description: Whether the investor was a lead investor

countryCode.description: Country code where the funding round occurred

state.description: State where the funding round occurred

city.description: City where the funding round occurred

roundLocation.description: Location where the funding round occurred

investorCount.description: Total number of investors in this funding round

nextCursor.description: Pagination cursor for the next page. Null if there are no more results.

post.description:
Maximum-coverage contact reveal — runs all waterfall steps in parallel to get the most comprehensive results. This is asynchronous: call this endpoint to start the task, then poll /contact-details/exhaustive/poll with the returned task ID. Slower and more expensive than the synchronous endpoints, but returns more emails and phone numbers on average. For faster synchronous results, use /contact-details/single (standard) or /contact-details/turbo/sync (fastest). ⚡ Rate limit: 60 requests per 1 minute 💰 Cost: Pay only for the data you request (exhaustive mode):
• 12 credits for all phone numbers AND all emails
• 5 credits for work email only
• 5 credits for personal email only
• 4 credits for phone only
• 9 credits for all emails ⓘ

post.description: Search LinkedIn posts using keyword-based queries. Returns a paginated list of posts matching the search criteria, up to 50 per page. **Keyword Search Syntax:** - **Exact phrase:** Wrap keywords in quotes for exact phrase matching. "head of sales" matches the exact phrase, not the individual words. - **AND:** Use **AND** between keywords to require both terms. sales **AND** engineering matches posts containing both words. - **OR:** Use **OR** between keywords to match posts containing any of the terms. sales **OR** marketing matches posts with either word. - **NOT:** Use **NOT** before a keyword to exclude posts containing that term. sales **NOT** recruiter matches posts with "sales" but without "recruiter". - **Parentheses:** Group terms to control operator precedence. (sales **OR** marketing) **AND** "series A" finds posts about either sales or marketing that also mention "series A". **Order of precedence:** 1. **Quotes (" "):** Exact phrase match. Phrase matching occurs before any Boolean logic is applied. 2. **Parentheses (()):** Used to explicitly group Boolean logic. Grouped expressions are evaluated before ungrouped logic. 3. **NOT:** Applied after any parentheses or quoted phrases are resolved. 4. **AND:** Evaluated after **NOT** but before **OR**. 5. **OR:** Lowest precedence among Boolean operators. ⚡ Rate limit: 60 requests per 1 minute 💰 Cost: 2 credits per page of results ⓘ

post.summary: Search companies and prospects from text
post.description:
Takes free-form text (e.g., 'Senior Product Managers from Series A to C FinTech startups in New York') and produces standardized filters (industries, funding stages, headcount ranges, locations, titles, seniorities, etc.). When limits are provided, executes the search and returns matching companies and people in a single synchronous call. When referencing specific companies, provide the identifier in one of these forms: plain name (e.g. 'Apple'), domain (e.g. 'apple.com'), or LinkedIn slug (e.g. 'company/banco-santander').Note: This is not optimized for job descriptions. If you have a JD, use the Search profiles from a job description endpoint instead. ⚡ Rate limit: 20 requests per 1 minute 💰 Cost: Fixed costs per request:
• 2 credits for company search params generation based on prompt, if required
• 2 credits for profile search params generation based on prompt, if required

Additional credits are charged for each company and profile returned, based on the search results. ⓘ ⏱ Recommended timeout: 1 minute ⓘ

Fixed costs per request:
• 2 credits for company search params generation based on prompt, if required
• 2 credits for profile search params generation based on prompt, if required

Additional credits are charged for each company and profile returned, based on the search results.

post.description: Create a new saved search. Given search params, it automatically re-runs it periodically and tells you which new people and/or companies fit your parameters over time (and also who drops out or returns). You are charged for each new prospect or company we find, depending on your desired type. You can also manually run the saved search if you don't want to wait for the next auto-run. ⚡ Rate limit: 10 requests per 1 minute 💰 Cost: 2 credits per prospect/company found in search ⓘ

otherContext.description: Any other disambiguating information or identifiers for the company, such as "YC startup" or "Italian airline"

description.description: A description of the company, such as what it does or its industry focus.

companyInfo.description: List of companies to look up. Max 400 companies can be provided at a time.

domainAgentRunId.description: The ID of the domain agent run. Provide this to the polling endpoint to get the actual results back.

post.description: AI-powered natural language search across multiple sources (LinkedIn, Google Maps, web, and more). Ideal for local business search where companies/employees have spotty web or LinkedIn presence. **Pagination flow:** 1. **First page** — send `{ search: { request: "initial", query: "...", pageSize: 10 } }`. The `pageSize` you choose here is locked for the entire session. 2. **Subsequent pages** — send `{ search: { request: "subsequent", cursor: "" } }`. 3. When `nextCursor` is `null` in the response, there are no more results. ⚡ Rate limit: 100 requests per 1 minute 💰 Cost: Pricing is coming soon. Credits will be charged once this feature is fully released. ⓘ

request.description: Use "initial" for the first page of a new search. Provide query, pageSize, and any filters.

query.description: Natural language search query, e.g. "pizza shops in NYC" or "Series A SaaS founders in London". The API infers whether to return companies or people.

pageSize.description: Number of results per page (default 10, max 1000). This value is locked for the entire pagination session.

country_codes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes (e.g. USA, GBR).

min_relevance.description: Minimum relevance score (0.0–1.0). Higher values mean a closer match to your query.

funding_stages.description: Last funding round stage filter. Acquired, public, closed, and unknown stages are not supported.

employee_growth.description: Year-over-year employee growth trend. Elements are OR-ed together.

website_traffic.description: Monthly website traffic bucket filter. Elements are OR-ed together.

employee_count.description: Filter by number of employees (inclusive range).

founded_year.description: Filter by company founding year (inclusive range).

is_b2b.description: If `true`, include only B2B companies. If `false`, exclude B2B companies.

is_tech.description: If `true`, include only tech companies. If `false`, exclude tech companies.

is_saas.description: If `true`, include only SaaS companies. If `false`, exclude SaaS companies.

is_startup.description: If `true`, include only startup-stage companies. If `false`, exclude startups.

website_traffic_growth.description: Year-over-year website traffic growth trend. Elements are OR-ed together.

has_linkedin_page.description: If `true`, include only companies with a LinkedIn page. If `false`, exclude them.

has_employees_on_linkedin.description: If `true`, include only companies that have employees listed on LinkedIn. If `false`, exclude them.

has_public_emails.description: If `true`, include only companies with public contact emails. If `false`, exclude them.

has_company_phone.description: If `true`, include only companies with a phone number. If `false`, exclude them.

hiring_is.description: If `true`, include only companies that are currently hiring. If `false`, exclude them.

is_ai.description: If `true`, include only AI-related companies. If `false`, exclude them.

companyFilters.description: Optional filters applied on top of the AI-derived company filters (e.g. country, funding stage, employee count, etc).

country_codes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes (e.g. USA, GBR).

min_relevance.description: Minimum relevance score (0.0–1.0). Higher values mean a closer job-title match.

include.description: Job titles to search for. Abbreviations are supported (e.g. 'CTO'). Elements are OR-ed together.

exclude.description: Job title keywords to exclude from results.

max_people_per_company.description: Maximum number of people to return per matched company.

company_linkedin_ids.description: Restrict results to people from these companies. Provide the numeric LinkedIn company IDs returned by Fiber's company search endpoints.

peopleFilters.description: Optional filters applied on top of the AI-derived people filters (e.g. job titles, country, max people per company). Only used when the query resolves to a people search.

request.description: Use "subsequent" for page 2 and beyond. Only the cursor from the previous response is required; all other parameters are stored server-side.

cursor.description: The `nextCursor` value returned by the previous response. Valid for 3 days.

x-credit-cost.description: Pricing is coming soon. Credits will be charged once this feature is fully released.

name.description: Company name

domain.description: Company domain

linkedinUrl.description: LinkedIn company page URL using the numeric company ID (e.g. https://linkedin.com/company/1234). Null if unavailable.

industry.description: Primary industry. The value comes from the data provider and may vary in format.

countryCode.description: Company country (ISO alpha-3 code, e.g. USA)

linkedinUrl.description: LinkedIn profile URL

countryCode.description: Person's country (ISO alpha-3 code, e.g. USA)

companyLinkedinUrl.description: The person's current company LinkedIn URL

companyCountryCode.description: The person's current company headquarters country (ISO alpha-3 code, e.g. USA)

data.description: Search results — either companies or prospects, never both

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Pass this as `cursor` in a `{ request: "subsequent", cursor: "..." }` request. `null` means there are no more results. Cursors expire after 3 days.
